investigations.name: dynamic-networks
investigations.title: Dynamic Networks — a catalog of network-reconfiguring rules
investigations.description: This investigation is a catalog: each study instantiates the same generalized process with a different registered reaction and shows the network evolving under that rule as an interactive animation and a GIF. Family A (studies 1–8) covers the dynamics OF networks — rules that rewire topology. A later Family B will add continuous multi-species dynamics ON the networks (an SBML simulator at each node via viva-copasi, with transport/diffusion along edges).
investigations.question: How do different local rules reshape a network over time, and can a single process-bigraph process — driven by pluggable reactions — reproduce the canonical families of network dynamics, each with a clear visualization of the network evolving?
investigations.hypothesis: One generalized NetworkDynamicsProcess, reconfiguring a graph through process-bigraph _add/_remove structural reactions, can reproduce the signature topology of every classic dynamic-network model — random growth, preferential attachment, small-world rewiring, fitness, duplication-divergence, forest-fire, adaptive coevolution, and activity-driven temporal networks — distinguishable by emitted structural metrics and by eye in the animations.
